title: Quick accent sort by frequency not working

judgment.rationale: The uppercase Ω example supports a targeted case-identity sorting test. Related restart persistence already has a merged fix, but that does not establish that this per-character failure is handled.
evidence: The reporter describes Ω staying at its base position with frequency sorting enabled in 0.68.0; resetting sorting only temporarily helped.
A commenter reports short-lived ordering in 0.77.0 and links #32850.
Current PowerAccent.GetCharacters sorts before ToUpper, while SendInputAndHideToolbar increments usage for the selected displayed character.
PR #37577 merged persistence for #26034; #32130 separately concerns center selection.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce uppercase/lowercase usage identity separately from persisted-order loss before approving a narrowly scoped correction.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current lookup-before-case-conversion path suggests a distinct per-character issue not established as covered by the merged restart-persistence fix.

proposed_fixes.title: Use consistent character identity for frequency lookup and increment
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: an uppercase selection such as Ω increments the displayed uppercase string, but the next frequency sort looks up the lowercase mapping before ToUpper, so the saved count is not applied to that candidate.
plan: In PowerAccent.GetCharacters and SendInputAndHideToolbar, trace the candidate string used for lookup and increment for ω/Ω with Shift and Caps Lock.
Choose a consistent usage identity or perform case transformation before sorting, preserving the intended independent/shared-case behavior and existing usage data.
Add regression coverage for uppercase Greek, ordinary lowercase accents, multi-codepoint mappings and stable tie-breaking; do not mix in center-selection UX changes.
verification: Repeated Ω selections move the intended candidate according to the selected frequency policy on the next activation.
Check lowercase, Shift and Caps Lock, then restart; distinguish case-key mismatch from persistence and reset-setting behavior.

confidence.rationale: The current ordering and increment sequence directly matches the named uppercase symptom, but historical settings and runtime behavior were not reproduced.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent sometimes fails to promote frequently selected characters, specifically Ω; a later commenter also reports ordering reverting after a short time.
known_information: Frequency sorting is enabled and resetting it helped only temporarily.
The original report is 0.68.0; the later report is 0.77.0.
The issue is open and unassigned, not owned by an empty assignee.
Related #32850 and #33221 were closed into #26034; #37577 later merged restart-persistence support.
inferences: The Ω-specific symptom may be a case-sensitive usage-key mismatch rather than only missing disk persistence.
The later generic reset symptom could be separate; the merged persistence PR is not proof of complete resolution.
issue_context.analysis: There is enough evidence for a maintainer-side discriminator. Asking for generic logs would not resolve the ordering identity visible in the code.
initial_investigation: Read the report, full comment and paginated timeline, then inspected #32850, #33221, #32130 and #26034 and verified merged PR #37577.
Inspected GetCharacters, SendInputAndHideToolbar and SaveUsageInfo in src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccent.Core/PowerAccent.cs at main commit 3d6827a53a579ba9bedcf8d4bbda21348d78cbdb.
Inspected src/modules/poweraccent/PowerAccent.Core/Tools/CharactersUsageInfo.cs: usage uses string-keyed dictionaries and persists UsageInfo.json.
No interactive frequency or restart test was executed.

actions.label: Compare Ω and ω frequency tracking

reproduce.title: Separate case-key sorting from persistence
reproduce.version_requirement: Current build containing #37577; compare historical 0.68.0 only if the current test passes.
prerequisites: A test account with Greek characters enabled and frequency sorting on; preserve existing usage data.
steps: 1. Set selection to start from the left to isolate center-selection behavior.
2. Select ω repeatedly, reopen the toolbar and record its position.
3. Repeat with Ω using Shift and then Caps Lock; compare dictionary lookup and increment keys under a debugger.
4. Test the next activation without restarting, then exit normally and restart to separately verify persisted ordering.
5. Repeat with a lowercase accented character and a multi-codepoint uppercase mapping.
reproduce.expected_result: Usage lookup and increment refer to the same intended candidate identity; frequent selections remain correctly ranked both immediately and after restart.
